request.spec:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export tree people (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-tree"`). It downloads `tree.csv` with the header `sheet,name,grade,due-total`, then one line per person: this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets of the tree by sheet id. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works:**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree-people` (`rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree-people.GET.yml`), backed by `rollup/RespondWithTreePeople.java`. It finds the tree's sheets and works out the figures the same way the existing tree search does. Each person's grade is the one in force on their own sheet's "today", and their due-total is what the screen shows, or `n/a` when there's no figure for them.
- **Front end:** `features/treeSearch/exportTree.slot.tsx` holds the button. It asks the server for the rows when pressed, so the file reflects what's stored at that moment. It uses the existing CSV helper, which quotes names containing commas or quotes.

No stored-data or schema changes were needed, and the export writes nothing to the audit file.
